title: ND Oracle Evidence Layer policy v1
principles: A source is not a conclusion.
Evidence roles apply to one exact claim, not globally to a source.
Authority about a source's own rules is not evidence that a service or intervention is effective.
Confidence applies only to exact claim wording and scope.
Contradiction, minority evidence and unresolved limitations remain inspectable.
Source count is an audit signal, not a truth vote.
Legacy v0.1 embedded sources remain authoritative until separately migrated; v1 does not duplicate them merely to increase top-level Evidence counts.

source_identity_or_availability.minimum: One current first-party source can be sufficient for a narrowly worded claim about the source's own identity, published feature, availability or access route.
source_identity_or_availability.corroboration: Required when the claim extends beyond what the source can authoritatively say about itself.
source_identity_or_availability.forbidden_shortcut: Do not convert existence, availability, popularity or marketing into efficacy, safety or personal fit.

legal_or_official_guidance.minimum: Current authoritative legislation, regulator or official guidance may support a bounded claim about what the rule or guidance says.
legal_or_official_guidance.corroboration: Independent legal interpretation or case authority is required for broader legal conclusions when wording or application is contested.
legal_or_official_guidance.forbidden_shortcut: Official status does not establish an individual entitlement or case outcome.

diagnostic_or_definition.minimum: Current authoritative clinical/diagnostic guidance plus appropriate synthesis where the claim goes beyond the text of one authority.
diagnostic_or_definition.corroboration: Expected for contested boundaries, biomarkers, differential diagnosis or cross-population generalisation.
diagnostic_or_definition.forbidden_shortcut: No checklist, single study, cognitive test or group difference becomes an individual diagnosis.

prevalence_or_frequency.minimum: Population, place, time period, sampling frame and measurement must be explicit; use representative datasets or appropriate epidemiological studies.
prevalence_or_frequency.corroboration: Expected when estimates vary materially across methods or populations.
prevalence_or_frequency.forbidden_shortcut: Reported experience frequency or community participation is not population prevalence.

association.minimum: Use appropriately designed observational evidence or synthesis with population/context explicit.
association.corroboration: Multiple studies or synthesis preferred for broad claims.

efficacy_or_benefit.minimum: Use comparative outcome evidence appropriate to the intervention and outcome; person-defined outcomes and adverse effects remain relevant.
efficacy_or_benefit.corroboration: Independent replication or synthesis is expected before a broad high-confidence efficacy claim.
efficacy_or_benefit.forbidden_shortcut: Testimonials, popularity, vendor claims or uncontrolled before/after descriptions are not sufficient.

safety_or_harm.minimum: Use safety-specific evidence, adverse-event data and relevant authoritative warnings where available.
safety_or_harm.corroboration: Expected for broad safety claims; absence of reported harm is not proof of safety.
safety_or_harm.forbidden_shortcut: Do not infer safety from effectiveness, popularity or lack of a warning.

mechanism.minimum: Use multiple converging evidence lines appropriate to the proposed mechanism.
mechanism.forbidden_shortcut: A plausible explanation or group correlation is not a demonstrated mechanism.

causation.minimum: Require designs capable of supporting causal inference and explicit treatment of plausible alternatives.
causation.corroboration: Strongly required unless the claim is extremely narrow and the design directly identifies causality.
causation.forbidden_shortcut: Temporal order or association alone is insufficient.

historical.minimum: Prefer primary/archival evidence, contemporaneous records or careful scholarship; represent date precision honestly.
historical.corroboration: Expected when attribution or exact dating is disputed.
historical.forbidden_shortcut: Do not turn the best current date candidate into an unqualified exact date.

product_or_service_feature.minimum: First-party documentation can support a current feature claim when commercial interest is explicit.
product_or_service_feature.corroboration: Independent evidence is required for usability, accessibility quality, efficacy, safety or personal-fit claims.
product_or_service_feature.forbidden_shortcut: Developer-declared accessibility metadata is not independent accessibility certification.

lived_experience.minimum: Published or appropriately governed experience evidence can support the fact and bounded pattern of reported experience.
lived_experience.corroboration: Use broader evidence for frequency, prevalence, mechanism or causation.
lived_experience.forbidden_shortcut: Experience is not automatically prevalence, mechanism or universality.

confidence.high: Strong support for the exact bounded proposition, with important contrary evidence considered and no known disagreement large enough to require material rewording.
confidence.moderate: Supported, but important limitations, indirectness, transfer problems or unresolved uncertainty constrain the proposition.
confidence.low: Some support exists but it is limited, indirect, fragile or under-replicated; wording must remain provisional.
confidence.contested: Credible evidence or interpretation materially disagrees; disagreement must remain visible.
confidence.not_applicable: Epistemic confidence is not the right descriptor for this record; it must not be used to evade evidence appraisal.
confidence.change_rule: A material confidence change requires evidence-backed rationale in provenance/commit history and must not silently erase earlier uncertainty.

source_quality.authoritative_guidance: Strong for what current official guidance/rules say; not automatically strong for effectiveness, causation or individual outcomes.
source_quality.peer_reviewed: Quality depends on design, measurement, population, analysis, replication and relevance; publication status alone is not a quality score.
source_quality.dataset: Strength depends on provenance, coverage, definitions, missingness, sampling and whether the dataset measures the claimed construct.
source_quality.community: Strong for the community's own stated position, service or reported experience; not automatically population-representative.
source_quality.lived_experience: Strong for the reported experience as reported; does not by itself establish frequency, mechanism or diagnosis.
source_quality.historical: Assess primary/secondary status, provenance, edition/version and date certainty.
source_quality.book: Treat as a source whose evidential role depends on genre, sourcing and the exact claim.
source_quality.commercial: Can establish current first-party product/service facts when conflicts are explicit; cannot independently establish efficacy or accessibility quality.
source_quality.practical: Useful for bounded practice description; evaluate authorship and basis before treating as evidence of outcomes.
source_quality.other: Requires explicit justification because the source class does not supply a default evidential expectation.

rules: Contradictory and falsifying contributions remain in the graph and are never deleted merely because other sources support the claim.
Source count must not be used as a majority vote.
Material contradiction triggers editorial review of claim wording, scope and confidence.
A Perspective is used for identifiable interpretation/framing; factual disagreement still requires claim/evidence treatment where ND Oracle evaluates it as factual.

provenance.role_change: A changed Evidence role requires a changed finding/rationale where appropriate and a provenance/commit-history explanation.
provenance.deprecation: Retracted, withdrawn or materially superseded sources are retained as deprecated historical records where the schema permits; claims are re-reviewed rather than silently rewired.
provenance.web_snapshots: Not mandatory by default. Consider an immutable snapshot/hash only for high-consequence mutable web evidence where exact wording matters and licensing/copyright/storage rules permit it.

discovery.ordinary_find: Evidence pages do not participate in ordinary practical /find/ ranking.
discovery.dedicated_evidence_browsing: Evidence inspection is static and local. Readers can use browser-native Find in page or browse the generated catalogue; no Evidence query is transmitted, stored or profiled.
discovery.privacy: Evidence browsing does not add a query service, analytics, profiling or network request.

requirements: Every governed claim has an evidence route and an explicit uncertainty route under its accepted schema model.
Every normalized v0.2 claim/evidence route is reciprocal at exact claim level.
Coverage registry includes every governed claim and every normalized Evidence object.
No normalized Evidence object is orphaned from a claim contribution.
Source-kind, contradiction, commercial-conflict, locator and negative semantic fixtures pass.
Public Evidence index and individual normalized/legacy evidence projections build without network access.
Ordinary discovery ranking, clinical boundaries, jurisdiction filtering, privacy and release-state gates remain unchanged.
